description: Killing parrots crashes your game. Note: I did kill other mobs and it isn t just swinging the sword and i got the same result everytime i killed a parrot. 19w40a: [^crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt] Description: Unexpected error java.lang.NullPointerException: Unexpected error at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at axx.f(SourceFile:1234) at dmq.a(SourceFile:363) at das.aE(SourceFile:1234) at das.aG(SourceFile:1517) at das.n(SourceFile:1367) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft version 19w40a.
2. Create or load any world in Creative mode with default settings.
3. Summon a parrot using the command `/summon minecraft:parrot ~ ~ ~`.
4. Equip a sword of any type.
5. Attack and kill the summoned parrot by right-clicking on it until its health reaches zero.
6. Observe that the game crashes after killing the parrot.
7. Repeat steps 3-6 multiple times to ensure consistency in the crash occurring every time a parrot is killed.

Note: The bug also occurs when killing other mobs, but the crash specifically happens consistently with parrots.
Observed Behavior: When killing parrots in Minecraft version 19w40a, the game crashes with a java.lang.NullPointerException. This issue occurs every time a parrot is killed and is not related to simply swinging the sword. The crash happens consistently regardless of other mobs being present or involved. The specific error message from the crash report indicates an unexpected error at `atd.a(SourceFile:407)` and traces through several source files, including `axx.f`, `dmq.a`, and multiple methods within `das`. This bug does not occur when killing other types of mobs, suggesting a unique issue with parrots. The attached crash report file is named "crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt" and provides detailed stack trace information that can help developers identify the root cause of this problem.
Expected Behavior: When attacking and killing a parrot with a sword, the game should not crash. The parrot should despawn normally without causing any errors or unexpected behavior. This should occur consistently in version 19w40a without leading to a java.lang.NullPointerException.
